questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Nowhere is the impact of automation more visible than in manufacturing.
Nowhere the impact of automation is more visible than in manufacturing.
Nowhere does the impact of automation is more visible than in manufacturing.
Nowhere the impact of automation more visible is than in manufacturing.
questions.explanation: 'Nowhere' at the start triggers inversion: 'Nowhere is the impact of automation more visible...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The auditor demanded that the records be made available immediately.
The auditor demanded that the records are made available immediately.
The auditor demanded that the records will be made available immediately.
The auditor demanded that the records being made available immediately.
questions.explanation: After 'demand that', formal English uses the subjunctive: 'the records be made available.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If the firm had invested earlier, it would now be a market leader.
If the firm invested earlier, it would now be a market leader.
If the firm had invested earlier, it will now be a market leader.
If the firm had invest earlier, it would now be a market leader.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result: 'If the firm had invested earlier, it would now be a leader.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Much as we value the partnership, we cannot accept these terms.
Much we value the partnership, we cannot accept these terms.
As much we value the partnership, we cannot accept these terms.
Much as we valuing the partnership, we cannot accept these terms.
questions.explanation: 'Much as' means 'although' in formal concession: 'Much as we value the partnership, we cannot accept...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It is not until profits stabilize that dividends will resume.
It is not until profits stabilize when dividends will resume.
It not is until profits stabilize that dividends will resume.
It is not until profits stabilizing that dividends will resume.
questions.explanation: The cleft structure 'It is not until...that' emphasizes timing: 'It is not until profits stabilize that dividends will resume.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The minister acknowledged that the policy had failed to meet its targets.
The minister acknowledged to that the policy had failed to meet its targets.
The minister acknowledged the policy failing to meet its targets that.
The minister is acknowledge that the policy had failed to meet its targets.
questions.explanation: 'Acknowledge' is followed by 'that + clause': 'acknowledged that the policy had failed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Judging by the latest figures, the recovery is gaining momentum.
Judge by the latest figures, the recovery is gaining momentum.
Judged by the latest figures, the recovery is gaining momentum, that.
Judging the latest figures by, the recovery is gaining momentum.
questions.explanation: 'Judging by' is a fixed participle phrase meaning 'based on': 'Judging by the latest figures, the recovery is gaining momentum.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A great deal of uncertainty surround the negotiations.
A great deal of uncertainty surrounds the negotiations.
A great deal of uncertainty surrounding the negotiations.
A great deal uncertainty surrounds the negotiations.
questions.explanation: 'A great deal of' + uncountable noun takes a singular verb: 'a great deal of uncertainty surrounds the negotiations.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Without the bailout, thousands of jobs would have been lost.
Without the bailout, thousands of jobs would been lost.
Without the bailout, thousands of jobs would have lost.
Without the bailout, thousands of jobs would have being lost.
questions.explanation: 'Would have been + past participle' expresses an unrealized past outcome: 'would have been lost.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The CEO, as well as the board, was informed of the breach.
The CEO, as well as the board, were informed of the breach.
The CEO as well the board was informed of the breach.
The CEO, as well as the board, informed of the breach was.
questions.explanation: With 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject only: 'The CEO, as well as the board, was informed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm purportedly falsified its safety records.
The firm purported falsified its safety records.
The firm is purportedly that falsified its safety records.
The firm falsified purportedly it its safety records.
questions.explanation: 'Purportedly' hedges an unconfirmed claim and sits before the main verb: 'purportedly falsified its safety records.'

questions.topic: Advanced relative clauses (on the grounds that)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The court rejected the appeal on the grounds that the evidence was insufficient.
The court rejected the appeal on the ground of that the evidence was insufficient.
The court rejected the appeal on grounds that of the evidence was insufficient.
The court rejected the appeal on the grounds which the evidence was insufficient.
questions.explanation: 'On the grounds that' introduces a formal reason clause: 'rejected the appeal on the grounds that the evidence was insufficient.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before had the industry witnessed such rapid consolidation.
Never before the industry had witnessed such rapid consolidation.
Never before did the industry had witnessed such rapid consolidation.
Never before the industry witnessed had such rapid consolidation.
questions.explanation: Fronting 'never before' triggers inversion: 'Never before had the industry witnessed such rapid consolidation.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The retention of key staff was a top priority during the merger.
The retain of key staff was a top priority during the merger.
The retention of key staff were a top priority during the merger.
The retaining key staff was a top priority during the merger.
questions.explanation: Formal writing nominalizes verbs: 'retain' becomes 'the retention of...'

questions.topic: Passive with modal perfect (cannot have been)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The results cannot have been calculated correctly given these figures.
The results cannot been calculated correctly given these figures.
The results cannot have calculate correctly given these figures.
The results cannot have being calculated correctly given these figures.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive expressing impossibility: 'cannot have been calculated correctly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some markets rebounded quickly; others, not at all.
Some markets rebounded quickly; others rebounded, not at all.
Some markets rebounded quickly; others is not at all.
Some markets rebounded quickly; others rebounds not at all.
questions.explanation: Ellipsis omits the repeated verb after a semicolon: 'others, not at all' (= others did not rebound at all).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The risk assessment changed. Accordingly, the premiums were adjusted.
The risk assessment changed, accordingly the premiums were adjusted.
The risk assessment changed. Accordingly the premiums were adjusted.
The risk assessment changed accordingly, the premiums were adjusted.
questions.explanation: 'Accordingly' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The results were disappointing. All the same, the board remained optimistic.
The results were disappointing all the same, the board remained optimistic.
The results were disappointing. All the same the board remained optimistic.
The results were disappointing, all the same board remained optimistic.
questions.explanation: 'All the same' means 'nevertheless' and begins a new sentence with a comma: 'All the same, the board remained optimistic.'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting a deadline extension?
options: I am writing to request an extension of the submission deadline.
Any chance we could push the deadline back a bit?
I am writing to request an extension of the submission deadline, cheers.
We're not gonna make the deadline, so extend it please.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to request an extension of the submission deadline' is a standard formal request.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about unauthorized charges?
options: I am writing to dispute a series of unauthorized charges on my account.
There are charges I didn't make and I want them removed now.
I am writing to dispute a series of unauthorized charges on my account, obviously.
Someone charged my account and I'm furious about it.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use precise, measured language such as 'I am writing to dispute...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The bank plans to roll out the new app nationwide next month.
The bank plans to roll the new app out of nationwide next month.
The bank plans to roll out of the new app nationwide next month.
The bank plans to roll the new app of out nationwide next month.
questions.explanation: 'Roll out' means 'to launch or introduce': 'roll out the new app nationwide.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The scandal left the company's reputation badly tarnished.
The scandal left the company's reputation badly tarnish.
The scandal left tarnished the company's reputation badly.
The scandal left the company's reputation badly tarnishing.
questions.explanation: 'Leave + object + past participle' shows a resulting state: 'left the company's reputation badly tarnished.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: All told, the campaign exceeded its fundraising target.
All telling, the campaign exceeded its fundraising target.
All tell, the campaign exceeded its fundraising target.
All told that, the campaign exceeded its fundraising target.
questions.explanation: 'All told' is a fixed absolute participle phrase meaning 'in total, considering everything.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm boosted short-term profits at the expense of long-term growth.
The firm boosted short-term profits at expense of long-term growth.
The firm boosted short-term profits at the expense for long-term growth.
The firm boosted short-term profits expense of at long-term growth.
questions.explanation: 'At the expense of' means 'to the detriment of': 'boosted profits at the expense of long-term growth.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The quarterly results failed to meet analysts' expectations.
The quarterly results failed to reach analysts' expectations meet.
The quarterly results failed to make meet analysts' expectations.
The quarterly results failed to meet of analysts' expectations.
questions.explanation: 'Meet expectations' is a fixed collocation: 'failed to meet analysts' expectations.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The council has significantly increased its infrastructure budget.
The council has increased significantly its infrastructure budget.
Significantly the council has increased its infrastructure budget.
The council significantly has increased its infrastructure budget.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of degree typically follow the auxiliary verb: 'has significantly increased.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The domestic market slowed. By contrast, exports grew strongly.
The domestic market slowed, by contrast exports grew strongly.
The domestic market slowed. By contrast exports grew strongly.
The domestic market slowed by contrast, exports grew strongly.
questions.explanation: 'By contrast' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: The trustees would hardly agree to such terms, would they?
The trustees would hardly agree to such terms, wouldn't they?
The trustees would hardly agree to such terms, don't they?
The trustees would hardly agree to such terms, do they?
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' makes the statement effectively negative, so the tag is positive: 'would hardly agree..., would they?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The rebrand was not entirely well received.
The rebrand was not all well received entirely.
The rebrand not was entirely well received.
The rebrand was entirely not well received.
questions.explanation: Formal understatement places 'not' before the adverb: 'was not entirely well received.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Had they not acted swiftly, the crisis would have deepened.
Had they not act swiftly, the crisis would have deepened.
They had not acted swiftly, the crisis would have deepened.
Had they not acted swiftly, the crisis will have deepened.
questions.explanation: 'Had + subject + not + past participle' is an inverted third conditional: 'Had they not acted swiftly, the crisis would have deepened.'
